claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers is controlled by the interplay of compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order.
Compositional complexity influences dislocation mobility in HEA multilayers.
Severe lattice distortion influences dislocation mobility in HEA multilayers.
Short-range order influences dislocation mobility in HEA multilayers.
Compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order influence deformation-twin formation.
The combined effects of compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order promote deformation-twin formation.
The combined effects of compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order pin dislocations.
Deformation-twin formation and dislocation pinning control progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading.
Increasing sustained loading increases deformation-twin density relative to the initial undeformed state.
Increasing sustained loading decreases dislocation mobility relative to the initial undeformed state.
The predicted increase in twinning and decrease in dislocation mobility produce a higher strain-hardening rate.
The predicted microstructural changes improve strength.
The predicted microstructural changes reduce ductility.
The individual contributions of compositional complexity, lattice distortion, and short-range order to deformation behavior are not well understood.
Failure to observe a correlation between deformation behavior, increased twin density, and decreased dislocation mobility would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction and falsification rule depend on decreased dislocation mobility, but the listed measurements include dislocation density rather than dislocation mobility, so the proposed experiment cannot directly apply its own falsification criterion.
